functions.name: score_targ
functions.sourceReview: Read the complete dogmove.c score_targ() body (738-837). The implementation preserves the confused-pet and quest-start short circuit, priest and minion alignment metadata, quest-friendly and coaligned-priest early returns, adjacency, tame-hero, and find_friends gates, hostility and passive penalties, weak-target and hero-relative level penalties, vampire-shifter strength roll, stronger-target penalty, level and hit-point score, final rnd(5) fuzz, and the confused-pet final rn2(3) penalty in C evaluation order. The source-valued state is supplied through the running game state; find_friends() and on_level() are existing source-aligned helpers, and no result-valued unported callee is substituted.

callers.source: dogmove.c best_target() calls score_targ(mtmp, temp_targ) at lines 870-871 while scanning each visible ray
dogmove.c pet_ranged_attk() calls best_target(mtmp, forced) at lines 907-911, which dispatches each candidate to score_targ()
dogmove.c dog_move() calls pet_ranged_attk(mtmp, FALSE) at lines 1273-1274; the JavaScript operation registry dispatches dog_move() through petRangedAttack

entryPointReview: The selected helper has one live production entry point: an active starting pet reaches dogmove.c dog_move(), which calls pet_ranged_attk(FALSE); pet_ranged_attk() calls best_target(), best_target() scans each visible ray and calls score_targ(), and the selected target reaches the existing monster-action attack path. The independently selected pet-ranged-score-probe recording executes this chain through the JavaScript dog_move() operation registry and includes score_targ() followed by mattackm() in one pet turn.
